nodes.label: Signal Tower (Creative North Star)
nodes.rationale: The tool should disappear; the interface exists to move content through a workflow, not to be noticed. Surfaces are quiet so the only color on screen is color that means something.

nodes.label: Tower Violet (#aa3bff)
nodes.rationale: Single action accent color at 295 degrees. Appears on primary buttons, focus rings, active nav. Its rarity is what gives it signal power. One Voice Rule: at most 10% of any screen.

nodes.label: Status Colors (Semantic Signal System)
nodes.rationale: Amber=pending, blue=approved, green=published, gray=draft/archived. Semantic only, never decorative. Status Purity Rule: these colors appear exclusively inside status badges tied to release lifecycle.

nodes.label: Flat-By-Default Elevation Rule
nodes.rationale: Depth through tonal value (gray-50 vs white), not shadow. Shadows appear only in renderer hover states. No box-shadow on static builder cards.

nodes.label: Renderer Exception (Typography Rule)
nodes.rationale: Builder body text is 14px for dense editing; renderer body is 18px for reading comfort. Different jobs, different comfort. The renderer is a communication surface, not a production environment.

nodes.label: One Voice Rule
nodes.rationale: Violet appears on at most 10% of any given screen. Two violet elements competing on the same screen is prohibited.

nodes.label: Retirement Rule (Indigo Banned)
nodes.rationale: indigo-600 (#4f46e5) and all Tailwind indigo-* values are retired. Violet (#aa3bff) is the canonical accent.

nodes.label: Approval Workflow (draft→pending→approved→published→archived)
nodes.rationale: PMs author content and route it through a 5-stage approval workflow. Success = published release that reached audience without a ticket to engineering.

nodes.label: Product Design Principles
nodes.rationale: 5 principles: Infrastructure over identity; Signal over noise; One voice at a time; Color means something; Legibility at speed.

nodes.label: Product Anti-References
nodes.rationale: Explicitly rejected: purple gradients, floating orbs, glassmorphism, hero-metric dashboards, SaaS-cream with soft shadows, maximalism, decorative elements, animation-heavy interfaces.

nodes.label: Register (Brand vs Product)
nodes.rationale: Every design task is brand (design IS the product) or product (design SERVES the product). Determines which reference file to load. First match: task cue, then surface, then PRODUCT.md register field.

nodes.label: Color Strategy Axis (Restrained/Committed/Full/Drenched)
nodes.rationale: Four commitment levels: Restrained (≤10% accent), Committed (30-60%), Full palette (3-4 roles), Drenched (surface IS the color). Use OKLCH. The 10% rule applies only to Restrained.

nodes.label: AI Slop Test
nodes.rationale: Two-altitude check: first-order (can you guess theme from category?) and second-order (can you guess aesthetic family from category+anti-references?). Both must fail before the design passes.

nodes.label: Absolute Bans (Impeccable)
nodes.rationale: Side-stripe borders, gradient text, glassmorphism as default, hero-metric template, identical card grids, modal as first thought. Match-and-refuse: if about to write these, rewrite with different structure.

nodes.label: Asset Buckets (produce/direct/semantic)
nodes.rationale: Every visual role is classified: produce (needs generation/cleanup), direct (ships as crop/conversion), semantic (build in HTML/CSS/SVG). Semantic does not mean ignored; includes concrete build handoff.

nodes.label: Adaptation as Rethinking (not Scaling)
nodes.rationale: Adaptation is rethinking the experience for the new context, not scaling pixels. Mobile needs thumbs-first design, touch targets 44x44px, bottom navigation.

nodes.label: Animation Timing Principles
nodes.rationale: Product: 150-250ms on transitions. Ease-out-quart/quint/expo. No bounce/elastic. Exit animations 75% of enter duration. Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Never animate layout properties casually.

nodes.label: Audit Dimensions (5-category 0-20 scoring)
nodes.rationale: Five dimensions each scored 0-4: Accessibility, Performance, Theming, Responsive Design, Anti-Patterns. Total /20. Bands: 18-20 Excellent, 14-17 Good, 10-13 Acceptable, 6-9 Poor, 0-5 Critical.

nodes.label: Bolder in Product Register
nodes.rationale: In product register, bold rarely means theatrics. It means stronger hierarchy, clearer weight contrast, one sharper accent, more committed density. Amplification is in clarity, not drama.

nodes.label: Brand Font Selection Procedure
nodes.rationale: 4-step procedure: write 3 brand-voice words, list 3 reflex fonts (reject if on ban list), browse real catalog with those words thinking of font as physical object, cross-check that final pick doesn't match original reflex.

nodes.label: Font Reflex-Reject List
nodes.rationale: Training-data defaults to ban: Fraunces, Newsreader, Lora, Crimson, Playfair Display, Cormorant, Syne, IBM Plex Mono/Sans/Serif, Space Mono/Grotesk, Inter, DM Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans, Instrument Sans/Serif, and others.

nodes.label: Aesthetic Lane Reflex-Reject List
nodes.rationale: Currently saturated aesthetic families: editorial-typographic (display serif + mono labels + ruled separators). Second-order slop trap: avoiding first reflex but landing in an obviously-adjacent aesthetic family.

nodes.label: Four-Gate Flow Before Code (Codex)
nodes.rationale: Steps A-D: direction questions, palette generation, mock generation, approval loop. Each ends with user stop. Shape confirmation alone is NOT a green light to code. Compressing gates is the dominant failure mode.

nodes.label: Working Memory Rule (≤4 items)
nodes.rationale: Humans hold ≤4 items in working memory (Cowan 2001). At any decision point: ≤4 manageable, 5-7 pushing limit, 8+ overloaded. Nav menus ≤5, form sections ≤4 fields, action buttons 1 primary + 1-2 secondary.

nodes.label: OKLCH Color Space Principle
nodes.rationale: Use OKLCH not HSL. Perceptually uniform: equal lightness steps look equal. Reduce chroma as lightness approaches 0 or 100. Tint neutrals toward brand hue (0.005-0.015 chroma).

nodes.label: Production Bar (Craft Definition of Done)
nodes.rationale: Real content, semantic HTML, deliberate spacing, intentional typography, realistic state coverage, finished interaction quality, coherent icon set, respect build pipeline, optimized imagery, premium motion, maintainable, technically clean.

nodes.label: Dual Assessment (Design Review + Detector)
nodes.rationale: Assessment A (design review) and Assessment B (detector/browser) run independently. A finishes before B's output enters synthesis context. Detector is deterministic but anchors judgment, not proof of completion.

nodes.label: Delight at Specific Moments (Product)
nodes.rationale: In product register, delight at specific moments only: completion, first-time actions, error recovery, milestone crossings. Reliability and consistency carry the rest. Delight everywhere reads as noise.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md Format (Google Stitch Spec)
nodes.rationale: Six fixed sections in exact order: Overview, Colors, Typography, Elevation, Components, Do's and Don'ts. YAML frontmatter is machine-readable layer. Tokens normative; prose provides application context.

nodes.label: Nielsen's 10 Usability Heuristics
nodes.rationale: Framework for evaluating usability across ten dimensions: visibility of system status, match between system and real world, user control and freedom, consistency and standards, error prevention, recognition over recall, flexibility and efficiency, aesthetic and minimalist design, error recovery, and help and documentation. Scored 0-4 per heuristic for a maximum total of 40.

nodes.label: Issue Severity Scale (P0–P3)
nodes.rationale: P0 = blocking/showstopper, P1 = major fix before release, P2 = minor annoyance with workaround, P3 = polish if time permits. Decision rule: would a user contact support? If yes, at least P1.

nodes.label: Eight Interactive States
nodes.rationale: Every interactive element requires: Default, Hover, Focus, Active, Disabled, Loading, Error, Success. Common miss: designing hover without focus. Keyboard users never see hover states.

nodes.label: Focus Ring Design
nodes.rationale: Never remove outline without replacement. Use :focus-visible to show ring only for keyboard users. Min 3:1 contrast, 2-3px thick, offset from element.

nodes.label: Popover API
nodes.rationale: Native browser API for tooltips, dropdowns, and non-modal overlays. Benefits: light-dismiss (click outside closes), proper stacking, no z-index wars, accessible by default. Places element in top layer.

nodes.label: CSS Anchor Positioning API
nodes.rationale: Tether overlay to trigger without JavaScript. Uses position: fixed to escape overflow clipping. @position-try handles viewport edges. Chrome 125+, Edge 125+; fallback needed for Firefox/Safari.

nodes.label: Roving Tabindex Pattern
nodes.rationale: For component groups (tabs, menu items, radio groups), one item is tabbable; arrow keys move within. Tab moves to next component entirely.

nodes.label: Spacing System (Layout)
nodes.rationale: Consistent scale is more important than specific values. Name tokens semantically (--space-xs through --space-xl). Use gap for sibling spacing. Apply clamp() for fluid spacing on larger screens.

nodes.label: Flexbox vs Grid Decision Rule
nodes.rationale: Flexbox for 1D layouts (nav bars, button groups, component internals). Grid for 2D layouts (page-level structure, dashboards). Don't default to Grid when Flexbox with flex-wrap is simpler.

nodes.label: Live Mode Poll Loop Contract
nodes.rationale: Strict execution order: boot live.mjs, navigate to app URL, run poll loop with 600000ms timeout. Events: generate -> plan 3 variants -> reply done; accept/discard -> clean up; exit -> cleanup. Carbonize accepts require cleanup before next poll.

nodes.label: Live Mode Identity Extraction (Phase A)
nodes.rationale: Non-skippable phase. Extract identity from: DESIGN.md > CSS custom properties > computed styles > sibling components. Record as one concrete sentence: dominant colors by hex, type pairing by font names, layout topology, surface treatment, voice tone. No aesthetic adjectives.

nodes.label: Live Mode Variant Parameters System
nodes.rationale: 0-4 params per variant as JSON on data-impeccable-params attribute. Three kinds: range (CSS var --p-<id>), steps (data attribute data-p-<id>), toggle (both). Budget scales with visual weight: leaf=0, small=0-1, medium=target 2, large=target 2-3 up to 4.

nodes.label: Motion Duration 100/300/500 Rule
nodes.rationale: 100-150ms instant feedback; 200-300ms state changes; 300-500ms layout changes; 500-800ms entrance animations. Exit animations ~75% of enter duration. Timing matters more than easing.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion (prefers-reduced-motion)
nodes.rationale: Not optional. Vestibular disorders affect ~35% of adults over 40. Provide crossfade or no-motion alternatives. Preserve functional animations (progress bars, loading spinners) but remove spatial movement.

nodes.label: Perceived Performance Principles
nodes.rationale: 80ms threshold: brains buffer ~80ms so under 80ms feels instant. Shift passive to active waiting: preemptive starts, early completion, optimistic UI. Too-fast responses can decrease perceived value for complex operations.

nodes.label: Onboarding Time to Value Principle
nodes.rationale: Get users to aha moment ASAP. Front-load the 20% that delivers 80% of value. Teach features when users encounter them (context over ceremony). Progressive disclosure, not a upfront dump.

nodes.label: Empty State Design Patterns
nodes.rationale: Five types: first-use (emphasize value, provide template), user cleared (light touch), no results (suggest query), no permissions (explain and path forward), error state (retry). Every empty state needs: what will be here, why it matters, how to get started, visual interest, contextual help.

nodes.label: Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID/INP, CLS)
nodes.rationale: LCP < 2.5s (optimize hero images, inline critical CSS, preload). FID < 100ms / INP < 200ms (break long tasks, defer non-critical JS). CLS < 0.1 (set dimensions on images/video, use aspect-ratio, don't inject content above existing).

nodes.label: Layout Thrashing Prevention
nodes.rationale: Batch DOM reads then DOM writes. Alternating read/write forces reflows. Use content-visibility:auto for long lists, virtual scrolling for very long lists.

nodes.label: Overdrive Browser Technology Toolkit
nodes.rationale: Cinematic transitions: View Transitions API, @starting-style, spring physics. Scroll-driven: animation-timeline:scroll(). Beyond CSS: WebGL, WebGPU, Canvas 2D/OffscreenCanvas, SVG filter chains. Performance: Web Workers, WASM, virtual scrolling.

nodes.label: Five Design Test Personas
nodes.rationale: Alex (impatient power user): efficiency and shortcuts. Jordan (confused first-timer): guidance at every step. Sam (accessibility-dependent): screen reader/keyboard only. Riley (deliberate stress tester): edge cases and gaps. Casey (distracted mobile user): one-handed thumb-zone.

nodes.label: Design System Discovery (Polish)
nodes.rationale: Aligning to design system is not optional. Identify drift by root cause: missing token, one-off implementation, or conceptual misalignment. Fix differs by category. Polish without alignment is decoration on top of drift.

nodes.label: Information Architecture & Flow (Polish)
nodes.rationale: Match experience shape to system: same progressive disclosure depth, same flow patterns (modal vs full-page, inline vs route, save-on-blur vs explicit submit), same naming and mental model across screens.

nodes.label: Product Slop Test
nodes.rationale: Would a user fluent in best tools (Linear, Figma, Notion, Raycast, Stripe) trust this interface or pause at subtly-off components? Failure mode: over-decorated buttons, mismatched form controls, gratuitous motion, display fonts in labels, invented affordances for standard tasks.

nodes.label: Product Color Strategy (Restrained default)
nodes.rationale: Product defaults to Restrained. Accent for primary actions, current selection, and state indicators only, not decoration. State-rich semantic vocabulary: hover, focus, active, disabled, selected, loading, error, warning, success, info.

nodes.label: Quieter Refinement Strategy
nodes.rationale: Reduce saturation to 70-85%, soften palette, reduce color variety, tinted grays (not pure gray). Reduce font weights, increase whitespace, remove decorative elements. Quiet without intent collapses to generic. Think luxury, not laziness.

nodes.label: Mobile-First Responsive Design
nodes.rationale: Start with base styles for mobile, use min-width queries to layer complexity. Content-driven breakpoints, not device sizes. Three breakpoints usually suffice (640, 768, 1024px). Detect input method (pointer/hover media queries), not just screen size.

nodes.label: Design Brief Structure (Shape)
nodes.rationale: 10-section brief: Feature Summary, Primary User Action, Design Direction (color strategy + scene sentence + named anchors), Scope (fidelity/breadth/interactivity/time), Layout Strategy, Key States, Interaction Model, Content Requirements, Recommended References, Open Questions. Must confirm before implementation.

nodes.label: Visual Direction Probe (Shape Phase 1.5)
nodes.rationale: Generate 2-4 visual direction probes when work is net-new or directionally ambiguous, fidelity is mid-fi+, and native image generation is available. Probes differ in hierarchy/topology/density/typographic voice/color strategy, not just palette tweaks.

nodes.label: 4pt Spacing Base System
nodes.rationale: 4pt base (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96px) preferred over 8pt; 8pt is too coarse. Semantic token names by relationship (--space-sm) not value (--spacing-8). Use gap over margins to eliminate margin collapse.

nodes.label: Container Queries
nodes.rationale: Viewport queries for page layouts. Container queries for components. container-type: inline-size on parent, then @container (min-width: Xpx) on child. Same card behaves differently in narrow sidebar vs wide main area without viewport hacks.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md Format (Strategic Context)
nodes.rationale: Sections: Register (brand|product bare value), Users, Product Purpose, Brand Personality, Anti-references, Design Principles (strategic 3-5 principles, NOT visual rules), Accessibility & Inclusion. Never overwrite without confirmation.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md Format (Visual Context)
nodes.rationale: Follows Google Stitch DESIGN.md format. Visual system: colors, typography, components, layout. Answers how it looks. Paired with PRODUCT.md. Every impeccable command reads both before work.

nodes.label: Typeset Register Strategy
nodes.rationale: Brand: fluid clamp() scale, >=1.25 ratio, pairing per brand lane. Product: system fonts and familiar sans are legitimate, one family typically carries whole UI, fixed rem scale, 1.125-1.2 ratio. Live-mode signature param: scale range 0.85-1.3.

nodes.label: Vertical Rhythm Principle
nodes.rationale: Line-height should be the base unit for ALL vertical spacing. If body text has line-height 1.5 on 16px type (=24px), spacing values should be multiples of 24px. Creates subconscious harmony via shared mathematical foundation.

nodes.label: Fluid Typography (clamp)
nodes.rationale: Use fluid type for headings on marketing/content pages. Use fixed rem for app UIs. Bound clamp: max-size <= ~2.5x min-size. Scale container width and font-size together to keep 45-75ch measure band at every viewport.

nodes.label: Web Font Loading Strategy
nodes.rationale: font-display:swap for visibility, match fallback metrics (size-adjust, ascent-override, descent-override) to minimize shift. swap=visible immediately with FOUT; optional=no shift if font misses ~100ms budget. Variable fonts for 3+ weights.

nodes.label: Button Label Pattern (Verb + Object)
nodes.rationale: Never use OK, Submit, Yes/No. Use specific verb + object: Save changes, Create account, Delete message, Keep editing. For destructive actions, name the destruction: Delete not Remove, show count.

nodes.label: Error Message Formula
nodes.rationale: Every error answers: (1) What happened? (2) Why? (3) How to fix? Don't blame the user. Templates: format error, missing required, permission denied, network error, server error.

nodes.label: Impeccable Shared Design Laws
nodes.rationale: Universal rules across brand and product registers: OKLCH color with tinted neutrals, four-step color commitment axis (Restrained/Committed/Full palette/Drenched), theme by physical scene sentence, typography hierarchy >=1.25 ratio, spacing for rhythm, motion ease-out-quart/quint/expo only. Absolute bans: side-stripe borders, gradient text, glassmorphism as default, hero-metric template, identical card grids, modal as first thought.

nodes.label: Impeccable Command Table
nodes.rationale: Categories: Build (craft, shape, teach, document, extract), Evaluate (critique, audit), Refine (polish, bolder, quieter, distill, harden, onboard), Enhance (animate, colorize, typeset, layout, delight, overdrive), Fix (clarify, adapt, optimize), Iterate (live).

nodes.label: Asset Producer Workflow (produce/direct/semantic)
nodes.rationale: Three buckets: produce (needs generative cleanup), direct (crop/convert/compress existing clean source), semantic (build in HTML/CSS/SVG/canvas, no raster). Semantic roles still require concrete implementation handoff. Never redesign, only produce from approved mock.

nodes.label: Adaptation Strategy (Rethink, Not Scale)
nodes.rationale: Adaptation is rethinking the experience for the new context, not scaling pixels. Mobile: single column, 44x44 touch targets, thumbs-first, bottom navigation. Tablet: hybrid approach, master-detail views. Desktop: multi-column, hover states, keyboard shortcuts.

nodes.label: Teach Flow — PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md Generation
Type Scale Strategy (fixed rem vs fluid clamp)
Live-mode Scale Parameter for Typography Variants
Button Label Pattern (verb + object, no OK/Submit)
P1: Indigo Accent Violates Design System (Retirement Rule)
P2: Hover-Only Actions — WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7 Violation
P2: Template A/B/C Unexplained — Replace with Descriptive Names
Users: Support Reps, Account Managers, Customer Success Managers
Builder App Favicon (Lightning Bolt Brand Icon)
Hero Image — Isometric Stacked Layers Illustration
Release Hub UI Icon Set (SVG Sprite)

edges.source_location: ## Step F: Asset Slicing via the Asset Producer

hyperedges.label: Release Hub Design Coherence: Product + Design System + Status Lifecycle
hyperedges.rationale: The 5-stage approval workflow directly drives the status color system, which is the visual heartbeat of the release table; all three form a coherent product-design contract.

hyperedges.label: Anti-Slop Enforcement: Absolute Bans + AI Slop Test + Reflex-Reject Lanes
hyperedges.rationale: These three concepts together form a layered defense against generic AI-generated aesthetics: absolute bans prevent specific patterns, the two-altitude slop test checks first- and second-order reflexes, and reflex-reject lanes identify currently-saturated aesthetic families.

hyperedges.label: Craft Visual Direction Pipeline: Codex Four Gates + Asset Producer + Production Bar
hyperedges.rationale: The four pre-code gates (codex.md steps A-D), the asset producer subagent (step F), and the production bar together form the complete craft flow from visual direction through to shippable code.

hyperedges.label: Identity Preservation System in Live Mode
hyperedges.rationale: All three nodes participate in the same identity-lock flow: live mode Phase A extracts identity by reading DESIGN.md (visual) and PRODUCT.md (strategic) as primary sources. Missing DESIGN.md never excuses skipping identity extraction; extract from CSS instead.

hyperedges.label: Polish Quality Gate (final pass pattern)
hyperedges.rationale: Multiple impeccable sub-commands (onboard, quieter, optimize, typeset, layout) all conclude by handing off to impeccable polish. Polish requires design system discovery and IA/flow alignment before any surface polishing work. These three nodes form the mandatory entry sequence for the final quality gate.

hyperedges.label: Register + Context File Pair
hyperedges.rationale: SKILL.md mandates loading PRODUCT.md (register, brand strategy) and DESIGN.md (visual system) before any design work. The register field in PRODUCT.md controls which reference file (brand.md or product.md) is loaded next. These three always participate together as the context-gathering bootstrap for every impeccable command.

hyperedges.label: Accessibility Requirements Cluster
hyperedges.rationale: All four nodes address different facets of the same accessibility requirement domain — reduced motion, keyboard visibility, and contrast — forming a group relationship that goes beyond any pairwise link.

hyperedges.label: AI Slop Rejection System
hyperedges.rationale: These four nodes collectively constitute the impeccable skill's anti-AI-slop system — each attacks the problem from a different angle (branding, fonts, audit detection, visual amplification), forming a system not captured by pairwise edges alone.

hyperedges.label: Craft Build Pipeline
hyperedges.rationale: These five nodes form the sequential craft build pipeline — shape, visual direction, palette, mock approval, and production bar — where the group relationship encodes an ordered workflow not represented by any single pairwise edge.

hyperedges.label: Impeccable Reference Suite — shared design quality system
Release Hub Product Identity — brand, users, design principles
